title: Calcium Carbonate (Industrial Grade)
description: High-purity calcium carbonate (CaCO3) — ground calcium carbonate (GCC) and precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) for construction, plastics, paints, food, and industrial applications in Oman.

details.longDescription:
Calcium carbonate (CaCO3, CAS 471-34-1) is the most widely used industrial mineral, and Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in two forms. Ground calcium carbonate (GCC) is limestone or marble milled to a controlled particle size, available from coarse to fine grades, typically with a D50 of 5–50 micron, 97–99.5% CaCO3, moisture below 0.5% and brightness of 92–96% ISO in coated and uncoated versions. Precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) is made chemically for higher purity and a controlled crystal shape, used where food, pharmaceutical or specialty-coating specifications apply. Food-grade E170 is available with the manufacturer's food-grade specification.

Which grade fits which job. Construction takes the coarser GCC as a filler in mortars, tile adhesives, putties and concrete, and as road base. Plastics compounders use fine GCC as the filler in PVC pipe and profile, polyolefin film and rubber at loadings up to 60%, where the oil absorption of 18–22 g/100 g governs how much plasticiser the compound needs. Paint makers use the bright, fine grades as an extender pigment that replaces part of the titanium dioxide. Paper mills use it as filler and coating pigment; adhesive and sealant producers as a rheology filler; animal-feed mills as the calcium supplement.

In water treatment, calcium carbonate neutralises acidic effluent without the overshoot risk of lime, and calcite contactors remineralise desalinated water, which matters across Oman because reverse-osmosis permeate is corrosive to pipes until calcium and alkalinity are restored. Food and beverage plants use E170 for calcium fortification and as an anti-caking agent.

Packs are 25 kg bags, 500 kg and 1,000 kg super sacks and bulk tanker for plant-scale users. The product is non-hazardous; keep bags dry because wet carbonate cakes and loses flow. A certificate of analysis giving CaCO3 content, particle size, brightness and moisture comes with every lot, and the food grade carries its compliance certificate. Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the grade, particle size, tonnage and delivery point.

faqs.question: What are the industrial uses of calcium carbonate in Oman?
faqs.answer: Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃, limestone, calcite, CAS 471-34-1) is one of the most widely consumed industrial minerals in Oman across multiple sectors. In water treatment, calcium carbonate is used for pH correction and water remineralisation — adding alkalinity to acidic desalinated water (produced by RO plants), which is corrosive without calcium and bicarbonate hardness, and for neutralising acidic wastewater in industrial effluent treatment. In construction, ground calcium carbonate is used as a filler in concrete, asphalt, and construction mortars, and as a coating pigment in paints. In Oman's oil and gas sector, calcium carbonate-based lost circulation materials (LCM) are used in drilling muds to seal fractured formations and prevent drill fluid loss. In agriculture, agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) corrects acidic soils and growing media, although most Omani soils are already calcareous. In manufacturing, calcium carbonate is used as a filler in PVC pipes (common in Oman construction), plastics, rubber, paints, and paper. Global Chemicals LLC supplies calcium carbonate in water treatment, industrial, and agricultural grades in bags and bulk.

faqs.question: What is the difference between precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) and ground calcium carbonate (GCC)?
faqs.answer: Ground calcium carbonate (GCC) is produced by mechanical grinding of natural limestone rock (calcium carbonate mineral) to produce particles of controlled size. Particle sizes range from coarse (100–1000 µm for water treatment and agriculture) to fine (1–45 µm for fillers in paint, plastics, and rubber). GCC retains the natural crystal form (calcite rhombohedra or aragonite) of the original limestone. Precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) is synthetically produced by carbonation of calcium hydroxide slurry — carbon dioxide is bubbled through milk of lime, precipitating CaCO₃ crystals. PCC can be manufactured in controlled morphologies (scalenohedral, rhombohedral, acicular) with very narrow particle size distribution and high surface area (15–25 m²/g vs GCC's 1–5 m²/g). PCC's controlled morphology makes it superior as a coating pigment in paper and pharmaceuticals, while GCC's lower cost makes it dominant in construction, water treatment, and agriculture. In Oman, GCC is the standard for water treatment pH correction and construction applications. Global Chemicals LLC supplies both GCC and PCC grades.
